clue.text: Employers may have a variety of ruses

indicators.note: a variety suggests the letters of the next word come in a different order

explanation.surface: Bosses are said to have all sorts of tricks up their sleeves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a variety of' signals an anagram of RUSES.
explanation.definitionFit: Anyone who employs a thing, such as a tool or service, is a person making use of it.

clue.text: Erica's minion?

parts.note: Erica is the botanical name for heather, also called ling; whoever ranks below it is its subordinate

explanation.walkthrough: Erica looks like a woman's name but is the heather genus; heather is also called ling, and a minion sits beneath its master.
explanation.definitionFit: A minion is a lowly subordinate, someone placed beneath a superior.

clue.text: Move carefully when on 50 to make a stand

parts.note: to ease something is to move it gently and carefully
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Advice to tread gingerly at fifty if you want to take a stand.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist's frame for holding a canvas upright is a kind of stand.

clue.text: He spared a replacement for men at the front

indicators.note: a replacement shifts things around, so these letters take new positions

explanation.surface: A man let a substitute off for the soldiers in the front line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacement' signals an anagram of HE SPARED A.
explanation.definitionFit: The leading troops in an attack form its point, the forward thrust.

clue.text: It's a bloomer to look clever

parts.note: to eye something is to look at it
bright means clever, as of a quick pupil

explanation.surface: Someone warns that trying to appear smart is a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' suggests a blunder, but here it is literally a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyebright is a small wild flower, a plant that blooms.

clue.text: Without iron, say

parts.note: ex means without, as in ex dividend
to press clothes is to iron them

explanation.surface: A note that something is lacking iron, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like 'for example' but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To put a thought into words is to voice or state it.

clue.text: Object about confounded bore being invested

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes round another

parts.note: an end is an object or aim

indicators.note: confounded means mixed up, so the letters of bore are jumbled

explanation.surface: A complaint about a tiresome person who has put money in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confounded' turns BORE into ROBE, and 'about' puts END around it.
explanation.definitionFit: To invest someone is to clothe them in ceremonial garb, as at an installation.

clue.text: This turns around or turns to the right

indicators.note: read from the right it gives the same letters as read from the left

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Something that spins round, or swings to the right.
explanation.walkthrough: The word reads the same in both directions, so turning it round to read from the right changes nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: The spinning part of a helicopter or engine is the component that revolves.

clue.text: Achieving success late in life

explanation.surface: Someone making it big only in old age.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing well means making progress; being elderly is also described by this phrase about advancing years.

clue.text: Body discovered in a bath in Glasgow!

indicators.note: discovered means found inside, so the letters sit within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A grim news story of a corpse found in a Scottish tub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Body' looks like a corpse but means an assembly, as a Norse parliament was called.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scandinavian parliament or assembly is a governing body.

clue.text: Colouring due to complaint

explanation.surface: Paint that is used because of an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Distemper is a water-based wall paint, and also a viral disease of dogs.

clue.text: The full playing staff are needed here

definitions.text: The full playing staff are needed here

parts.words: The full playing staff are needed here
parts.note: a musical direction for the whole orchestra to play together, staff hinting at a stave

explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' suggests employees, but the playing staff are the musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian musical term means all performers together.

clue.text: How to take the measure of a top man

explanation.surface: A way to size up the boss.
explanation.definitionFit: A measuring stick is one sense; a sovereign or leader who governs is the other.

clue.text: 7 with half of them sounding off

indicators.note: the second half of the word them is taken

parts.note: barking is loud noisy sounding off, as by a dog

explanation.surface: A cross-reference saying half of them are complaining loudly.
explanation.walkthrough: '7' refers to the solution of 7 Down, here in its sense of boarding a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Boarding a ship or vehicle is the act of stepping aboard.

clue.text: Bad feeling

parts.note: read not as ill will but as feeling physically unwell

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad feeling' suggests resentment, but here it means feeling poorly.
explanation.definitionFit: Sickness is the state of feeling unwell.

clue.text: Newly-built homes — a lot quite dreadful

indicators.note: newly built means constructed afresh, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A complaint that a big estate of new houses is awful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Newly-built' signals an anagram of HOMES and A LOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something detestable or repulsive is utterly dreadful.

clue.text: A medical attendant has a duty to ensure dryness

parts.note: Dr is short for doctor
ought expresses obligation or duty

explanation.surface: A doctor is obliged to keep things dry.
explanation.definitionFit: A long spell without rain is a period of dryness.

clue.text: Put in an awkward situation straight away

explanation.surface: Someone embarrassed immediately.
explanation.definitionFit: Being challenged to respond at once means being in a tight corner; it also means immediately.

clue.text: Forms opinion the duck is revolting

parts.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so O
to rise up is to revolt

explanation.surface: Someone decides that the duck is disgusting.
explanation.definitionFit: To speculate or hypothesise is to form an opinion.

clue.text: Nan makes an excellent scholar

parts.note: grand means splendid or excellent
MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate scholar

explanation.surface: A grandmother turns out to be a fine academic.
explanation.definitionFit: Nan is an informal word for a grandmother.

clue.text: Nobody could remember suffering from this

definitions.text: Nobody could remember suffering from this

parts.words: Nobody could remember suffering from this
parts.note: those afflicted cannot recall anything, including the affliction

explanation.definitionFit: Loss of memory is the condition described.

clue.text: Concentrated in time of action

parts.note: a verb's tense shows the time at which an action happens

explanation.surface: Focused when the moment for action comes.
explanation.definitionFit: Something strong and focused, of great force, is concentrated.

clue.text: Pressing for a little time

explanation.surface: Urgency for a short while.
explanation.definitionFit: Urgent or immediate is one sense; a moment is the other.

clue.text: Nowadays a chap hires supporters

parts.note: AD, anno domini, marks the present era
he is a chap, a male
to rent is to hire

explanation.surface: These days a fellow pays people to back him.
explanation.definitionFit: Followers or backers of a cause are its supporters.

clue.text: Like to accommodate the bishop with a wall-hanging

indicators.note: to accommodate is to house, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: as means like
RR, Right Reverend, is a bishop's title

explanation.surface: A bishop is housed alongside a tapestry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to accommodate' puts RR plus A inside AS.
explanation.definitionFit: A tapestry hung on a wall, named after a French town.

clue.text: Making gunmen an offer would be mad

parts.note: RA, the Royal Artillery, are gunners
a bid is an offer, as at auction

explanation.surface: Proposing a deal to armed robbers would be crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gunmen' suggests criminals, but the Royal Artillery are the soldiers who fire the guns.
explanation.definitionFit: Fanatical or furious is a sense of mad.

clue.text: The German soldiers both backed down

indicators.note: each of the two pieces is read backwards where it stands

parts.note: die is a German word for the
RE, Royal Engineers, are soldiers

explanation.surface: German troops both retreated and backed down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'both backed' turns DIE into EID and RE into ER, each in place.
explanation.definitionFit: The soft fine feathers of a sea duck are the source of down.

clue.text: It takes many about half a day — fancy!

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, a large number
re means about, concerning
AM covers the morning, half of the day

explanation.surface: Something takes most people about twelve hours, imagine that!
explanation.definitionFit: A fancy is a fantasy or reverie.

clue.text: Figure a Greek character should go to the doctor

parts.note: rho is a letter of the Greek alphabet
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: Advice that a Greek person should see a physician.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhombus, a parallelogram with equal sides, is a geometric figure.

clue.text: The perception of speed?

parts.note: keen perception, and also quickness, both suggest acuteness

explanation.definitionFit: Keenness of mind is perception; quickness is speed.

clue.text: Firm offering place without delay

parts.note: stead means place, as in instead
fast means quickly

explanation.surface: A company offering its premises immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like a company but is the adjective, resolute.
explanation.definitionFit: Steady and unwavering is firm.

clue.text: X's reading matter

explanation.surface: A cross's choice of reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The multiplication sign is read as a word meaning multiplied by, and a famous London newspaper is the reading matter.
